lyrics:
[Intro: twelve-string acoustic guitar arpeggio, distant ship's bell]

[Verse 1: raspy, storytelling, slow sway begins]
I won a ticket in a raffle that I don't recall
A white ship at the harbour wall, a brass band in the hall
A steward took my suitcase and he took my name
Said "everybody boards alone and nobody's to blame"

[Verse 2: bass and drums enter]
There were ladies at the railing in their evening best
There were gentlemen who'd loosened every button on their vest
I asked a man beside me how long he'd been at sea
He looked up at the mirror ball and didn't answer me

[Chorus: high harmonies, guitars answering]
Welcome aboard the Meridian
Such a beautiful night
Plenty of room on the Meridian
Any hour, the buffet's bright
They're dancing on the lido deck
They've danced there since the war
It's last call at the Meridian
It's been last call since before

[Verse 3: storytelling, a little uneasy]
The captain is a recording and the map's a painted wall
The clocks are all on different times and no one minds at all
I asked the purser "where's the port?" and he poured me wine
Said "sir, we have a schedule, and it's working out just fine"

[Chorus: high harmonies, guitars answering]
Welcome aboard the Meridian
Such a beautiful night
Plenty of room on the Meridian
Any hour, the buffet's bright
They're dancing on the lido deck
They've danced there since the war
It's last call at the Meridian
It's been last call since before

[Verse 4: quieter, the reveal]
I went below to find the door I'd come through at the start
Just a mural of a doorway, very tasteful, very smart
The band struck up my favourite and a chair slid out for me
I thought, one more and then I'll go
And I've been one more since

[Guitar Solo: two lead guitars trading phrases, then in harmony]

[Outro: twin guitars in harmony over the sway, long fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 74 BPM, 4/4, B minor. A slow sway with a hint of reggae in the guitar chops and a Spanish colour in the chords. Hazy, seductive and uneasy.

VOICE: Male tenor with a dry rasp, singing like a man telling a story across a table. High, smooth harmony voices join for the choruses. No vocal histrionics. The last line is delivered flat and quiet.

INSTRUMENTS: A twelve-string acoustic guitar playing the opening arpeggios. Two electric lead guitars, one bright and one thicker, which answer the vocal and then share a long harmonised duet. Electric rhythm guitar playing off-beat chops. A melodic bass. A relaxed drum kit with timbales and a soft backbeat. A ship's bell.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, twelve-string guitar. 0:26 Verse 1. 0:52 Verse 2, band in. 1:18 Chorus 1. 1:50 Verse 3. 2:16 Chorus 2. 2:48 Verse 4, quieter, ending on the reveal. 3:20 Guitar solo: the two leads trade four-bar phrases. 4:10 They join in harmony over the verse chords and play the tune out, fading by 5:00.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1970s Los Angeles studio rock: dry, wide and immaculate, acoustic and electric guitars carefully layered, drums soft and close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The two guitars locking into harmony at about 4:10.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: No one forbids him to leave. The ship is pleasant, the chair slides out, and he keeps choosing one more. That is the quieter trap of later life and of endless entertainment.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Curiosity, comfort, unease, contented surrender.
